Edge of Junk 2017

By: Graham Coetzer | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Amidst the last few weeks political upheaval, ratings agency S&P have downgraded South Africa to junk status

Unique Selling Point:
Coming hot on the heels of the President's decision to fire his minister of finance, ratings agency S&P have downgraded South Africa to junk status. If two of the top three do so, our investment grade will officially be junk status. We will examine the consequences for the country and the man on the street.

Summary:
We will unpack what that led to the ratings downgrade, as well as what it will mean for the country as a whole and the effect on the man on the street. We have confirmed interviews with the SACP, and economic and political analysts. We have asked for interviews from both the president and and deputy president. We have also requested an interview with Gwede Mantashe, who it seems might actually do the interview. We are also awaiting a response from former minister of finance Trevor Manuel. We will also be speaking to the DA who have launched a court application to try and have President Zuma's decision to sack the finance minister and his deputy declared illegal. We are also waiting for a response from Cosatu.

Dr. Iraj Abedian Economist
Mr. Solly Mapaila Dep Sec Gen SACP
Mr. Aubrey Matshiqi Political Analyst

Press Release:


SA’s sovereign credit rating downgraded to junk status
Just days after President Jacob Zuma reshuffled his cabinet and fired Finance Minister Pravin Gordhan and his Deputy Mcebisi Jonas, international ratings agency Standard
and Poor’s downgraded South Africa’s long-term currency sovereign credit rating to junk status. As experts count the cost of higher interest rates on bonds and vehicle
repayments for ordinary South Africans, Carte Blanche examines the consequences of being relegated to junk status.

Script:


Junk Status
7 April 2017

Voice
Last week, the country was left reeling after President Jacob Zuma’s midnight reshuffling of his cabinet. Foremost in everyone’s minds was the removal of Finance Minister Pravin Gordhan and his deputy Mcebisi Jonas.

Sound Up Pravin Gordhan (CBInsert Bloodbathpart 1 Joy Summers 2 April 2017)
Bongani: How were you told?
Pravin: I wasn’t told. I learnt through a tv screen.
Bongani: That’s extraordinary
Pravin: That’s life.

Voice
And then on Monday this week yet another blow to the national psyche. Standard and Poor’s had downgraded our sovereign credit rating to junk status. On Friday the same news followed from ratings agency Fitch.

Sound Up Iraj
As soon as two of the three rating agencies have downgraded us to below investment grade, typically known as junk grade, then we are at junk grade.

Voice
Economist Dr Iraj Abedian says this is a massive blow to the South African economy, because many sovereign funds will no longer be able to operate in South Africa.

Sound Up Iraj
They are not allowed to be in a country that has sub investment grade rating. So whether they like us or not, their rules don’t allow them to be, so they pull the plug. And anything from six weeks to six months they have to exit no matter what the cost.

Voice
Dr Abedian says that would mean literally billions of dollars leaving the country

Sound Up Iraj
That essentially means that South Africa’s access to the pool of global capital would shrink dramatically. And I mean dramatically.

Voice
Speaking at a press conference on Wednesday this week, new finance minister Malusi Gigaba admitted the recent cabinet reshuffle had played a major part in the first downgrade announced by S&P.

Sound Up Malusi Gigaba
The main reasons for the downgrade and the negative assessments by S&P include, the recent executive changes, which they say have put at risk fiscal and growth outcomes.

Link
Political instability, the Rand in free fall, the country’s credit rating has taken a massive hit, but what does this mean for ordinary South Africans who are trying to keep their heads above water?

Sound Up Iraj Abedian
Next month, sure as the sunshine will rise tomorrow your petrol prices will go up. All the new items on the shelves will be so much more expensive, simply because the price of transportation has gone up.

Voice
And the bad news doesn’t stop there. Dr Abedian predicts a rise in inflation within the quarter, and a whole host of knock on effects, like the cost of capital mounting and a rise in interest rates.

Sound Up Iraj Abedian
Your application today at the bank will be priced up. Businesses credit lines will go up. Immediately. Which means the cost of doing business in the country has gone up, which means the viability of doing business in the country has come down accordingly, which means job creation capacity has gone down.

Link Devi
President Jacob Zuma is the original survivor, and while he weathers every storm, the country is taking a beating. The question is who will come out on the other end, South Africa or our president?

Voice
The embattled president came under fire again this week, even from alliance partners such as the SACP. Second Deputy Secretary General Solly Mapaila said the ANC themselves should be driving the motion of no confidence against President Zuma in parliament.

Sound Up Solly
We are concerned that our comrades, should have been the ones that were driving this particular motion, particularly when there is a gross neglect of duties by the president. It should not have come from the opposition parties.

Voice
But many political commentators believe the motion of no confidence has little chance of succeeding, a view shared by analyst Aubrey Matshiqi.

Sound Up Aubrey Matshiqi
In the leadership structures of the ANC, the NWC and the NEC included, the balance still favors Jacob Zuma.

Voice
Although members of the ANC top six spoke out in public against the president last week, the party closed ranks at a press conference on Wednesday. Secretary General, Gwede Mantashe, who was one of the leaders who voiced concerns about the president’s axing of Pravin Gordhan, said there was an unprecedented development of officials of the ANC going public on their views on a particular matter.

Sound Up Gwede Mantashe
The point that we are making is that we must find it adult enough to close a door, beat each other up and if you find me with a blue eye I can develop a narrative that I bumped against a pole or something, rather than the leadership of the ANC going public on their disagreements.

Voice
He also said they accepted President Zuma’s explanation of a breakdown in his relationship with minister Gordhan .

Sound Up Gwede Mantashe
And the NWC has accepted the irretrievable breakdown of the relationship between the president and members of the cabinet as sufficient explanation for the decision taken by the president

Voice
The decision by the ANC’s national working committee came despite allegations that President Zuma had fired the finance minister based on a controversial intelligence report which supposedly claimed minister Gordhan was getting international investors to stand with him against the state.

Sound Up Solly Mapaila
It was based on the intelligence report, it was not much about working relationship. And in any case, the working relationship of comrades who are elected in their own right and who are selected on the basis of a criteria of the organization doesn’t necessarily have to be friends or buddies, it’s a working relationship and they must understand that. The president must actually man up to accept to work with people who differ with him.

Voice
The ANC denied that the report was the only reason the president sent minister Gordhan packing.

Sound Up Gwede
The issue of the intelligence report complicated the matter, creating a lot of unhappiness. This was consequently presented as the only reason for his removal, which was unfortunate and incorrect.

Sound Up Aubrey
It is going to be much easier for South African voters to remove the ANC from power in 2019 than it will be to remove Jacob Zuma as head of state.

Voice
While the political shenanigans continued, our banks credit ratings were also downgraded earlier this week.

Sound Up Iraj
Now what does bank downgrade mean? It means less credit available for the South Africa Inc. Whether an individual, a small business, a big business or government. So with comparison to last Thursday, today we have so much less capital available to our country.

Voice
The new minister of finance was still optimistic of our chances of preventing a second ratings agency downgrade at his press conference on Tuesday.

Sound Up Malusi Gigaba
Despite our current challenges, now is not a time for despondency. We have many strengths that we can leverage to grow our economy inclusively.

Voice
But scarcely a day later there would be more bad news for the economy, when National Treasury confirmed Director General Lungisa Fuzile, a man with more than 20 years experience at the department, had resigned.

Sound Up Iraj
The institution of National Treasury in South Africa, and in fact in all countries but in South Africa particularly since 1996, has been one of the pillars of our macro economic stability. That pillar is not so much about the ministers who come and go it’s about the institutional capacity, technocratic capacity, of that institution

Voice
And according to Dr Abedian, ratings agencies and investors get very nervous when men like Lungisa, suddenly resign.

Sound Up Iraj
So this problem that we have is not just a political one anymore, it’s now a very more basic one. Can we get a team at National Treasury who can quickly regain the institutional memory and the global network? Whoever comes in today, picks up the phone to some investment community, they don’t know whom she or he is. Whereas this team at National Treasury had 25 years of network.

Voice
While many analysts were taken aback by the President’s brazen firing of the former finance minister, Aubrey says it has been coming ever since Nenegate.

Sound Up Aubrey
For those who were willing to listen, the president has been making it clear since Pravin Gordhan was appointed, that he was not his choice. That he was imposed on him by what he called the real powers that be.

Sound Up Iraj
So that is where the political misjudgment has come on the part of the president. This is his biggest technical mistake, not political mistake, technically his lack of appreciation for how the capital markets work, how his treasury, our treasury, is dependant on borrowing for it’s cash flow requirements, therefore if this process is not managed professionally and I mean urgently, the government could end up in a situation where salaries cannot be paid, pensions cannot be paid, projects have to be put on hold and, and, and…

Voice
According to statements from both S&P and Fitch, the President’s reshuffle and axing of the former minister of finance are amongst the top reasons we’ve been downgraded as a country.

Sound Up Solly
We are quite clear that they had a very easy invitation on the basis of a reckless and irrational decision of our president to reshuffle in the manner that he did, in particular to remove the minister of finance Pravin Gordhan.

Link Devi
We’re not the first or the last country to endure political and economic turmoil. Others have learnt never to waste a crisis, and to rather use it as an opportunity to change things for the better.

Sound Up Aubrey
If we are to have another golden period as a country, what is important is the choices we make during this period of decline

Voice
And the new finance minister, who seems able to talk the talk will drive a lot of those choices: only time will tell if he can walk the walk.

Sound Up Malusi
I would like to reassure you that the fiscal trajectory our country has been pursuing, which I have been party to as a member of the National Executive will continue. Our fiscal objectives remain unchanged.

Voice
While that may be true, there is no escaping the inevitable realities that junk status will mean for the ordinary man on the street. We may be facing a recession in the next six months, so buckle up, it’s going to be a bumpy ride.

Sound Up Iraj
We are going to have a very tough economic condition. So avoid debt, if you have debt pay it back, as soon as you can, cut back on standard of living for now. You may be in a good job, comfortable, you may just find that at very short notice the company says we can’t keep it going, we’re closing down. Anything can happen, that’s just unfortunately the nature of recessionary milieu.
